Wait — the markings say "III" and "IIII" each enclosed in an oval. In OIML notation, ⅲ (iii) is class III (medium) and ⅲⅲⅲ (iiii... actually ⅲⅲⅲ is three marks?). The text says "accuracy class ⅲ or ⅲⅲⅲ" with markings "III" and "IIII". In the R76 convention, class III is marked as ⅲ and class IIII (special?) — actually the markings are III (3 circles = class 3) and IIII (4 circles = class 4). Hmm, actually the accuracy classes in non-automatic weighing instruments: special I, II, III, IIII. The oval-enclosed numbers indicate the number of verification scale intervals. So classes are III (3) and IIII (4). The Unicode ⅲ = roman numeral three, ⅲⅲⅲ appears to be... hmm, that's odd. The OCR says "ⅲ or ⅲⅲⅲ" — perhaps the original text was "III or IIII" where "IIII" is rendered as ⅲⅲⅲ... no wait, ⅲⅲⅲ would be III (three). Actually ⅲⅲⅲ is 3 characters = III. Hmm, but the note clarifies: accuracy class markings: "III" and "IIII", each enclosed in an oval. So the classes are III and IIII.

For accuracy_classes in the recommendation: ["III", "IIII"].

It's not varying per config with different values; it's just stating both configurations allowed. I'll record as type_level with value string ["Single interval", "Multi-interval"]? Hmm, the schema says value can be number | {min,max} | string. For a list... I could do value: "Single interval, Multi-interval". Let me keep it simple: "single_or_multi_interval" with value string.

Actually, maybe better: weighing_range_type: {value: "Single interval or Multi-interval"}. Hmm. I'll use value as string.

- Maximum number of weighing ranges: 2
- Tare: T ≤ -50% + e for single range; T ≤ -Max1 + e1 for multi-interval → this is config-dependent. Could be config_level with axis "weighing_range_count" (single vs multi). Values:
  - condition: "instruments with one weighing range", value: "-50% + e" — this is a formula. Keep as string: "T ≤ -50% + e"? Per rules, formulas kept as string. But unit? The -50% part... it's mixed. I'd keep value as string "T ≤ -50% + e" hmm. Let me record as config_level:
  - attribute: "tare_limit", axis: "weighing_range_configuration"
    - {condition: "one weighing range", value: "-50% + e"} — hmm, formula. Or record as negative tare limits. I'll keep formulas as strings.
    - {condition: "multi-interval", value: "-Max1 + e1"}
  
  Actually maybe simpler to keep tare in type_level as a string describing both. The schema has config_level for attributes varying by configuration. Tare limit varies by configuration (single vs multi-interval). I'll use config_level.

  - power_supply_type: "AC"

- Software identification — Version number: 10xxx (x = 0…9) → string value "10xxx" with description. Canonical label: software_identification_version_number, value: "10xxx", maybe note x = 0...9. Value as string "10xxx (x = 0…9)". Hmm — keep value "10xxx" and maybe include the parenthetical. I'll do value: "10xxx" — but the (x = 0…9) is part of it. I could include as string "10xxx (x = 0...9)". Let me just include the full string to not lose info. Actually canonical labels shouldn't have trailing punctuation; value strings can. Model family: The Max range 6–30 kg — is this a family of models with varying Max? The cert says "6 kg ≤ Max ≤ 30 kg" which is a range for the type, not discrete models. So no model_family needed — it covers a type S2 with a capacity range. Type-level with min/max is appropriate.
